headline: Single-cell and bulk multi-omics resolve immune and tumor cell states in cancer
label: Immune Cell State Multiomics
summary: Integrating scRNA-seq with bulk transcriptomic and TCR data is now linking defined immune and malignant cell states to prognosis and immunotherapy response.
synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-state resolution from single-cell RNA-seq, anchored to bulk cohort transcriptomics and then reduced to prognostic or response-predictive signatures via machine learning or WGCNA. In head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, a progression-associated tumor-reactive T-cell signature highlights ICOS-high CD8 T-cell functional states tied to immunotherapy response. In acute myeloid leukemia, an M2 macrophage subcluster underlies an 18-gene risk signature, while a neutrophil-centric inflammatory network is linked to a LASSO Cox inflammatory risk score. Prostate cancer work describes an FEV-associated metastasis-initiating-like state within immune niche remodeling, and a coexisting DCIS and IDC multi-omics study profiles cellular states and microenvironmental remodeling. What is new is the attempt to tie cell-state resolution to specific, testable candidates, though most items remain biomarker-oriented rather than mechanistic.
